slots.brief: Two balls thrown vertically from the same point one after another meet at a common height; find the time interval between throws or the meeting height.
A car decelerating uniformly covers the last half of a distance in a given time; find total time or initial velocity using two kinematic equations.
Coulomb-force analogy question: two protons repel with a given force; ask for force at a new separation or force between alpha particles at the same separation.
A body starts from rest with constant acceleration; use v-u relation plus displacement relation to find distance in a particular second or velocity at a marked point.

slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated particles
slots.brief: Compare de Broglie wavelengths of an electron and a proton accelerated through the same potential difference.
Projectile given range and maximum height; solve the two trajectory equations to find launch speed and angle of projection.
A block slides from rest down a curved frictionless track onto a rough horizontal stretch; use energy conservation plus work-energy theorem to find where it stops.
A man walks in rain falling vertically; find how umbrella angle changes when he runs faster, using relative-velocity vector construction.
Two identical speakers (or coherent sources) with given path difference at a point; decide constructive/destructive interference and compute resultant intensity ratio.
YDSE with one slit narrowed so amplitudes are in a given ratio; find the ratio of maximum to minimum intensity using I = 4I₀cos²(φ/2).
Three point charges fixed at corners of an equilateral triangle; find the force on one charge by vector-adding Coulomb contributions from the other two.
A particle in SHM passes two marked positions with given speeds; set up energy conservation to find amplitude and then time between positions via phase.

slots.subtopic: Moment of inertia of point masses
slots.brief: Four point masses fixed at the corners of a square; compute moment of inertia about a given axis (diagonal or through centre) as a sum of mr² terms.
A pendulum bob released from horizontal; find speed and tension in the string at the lowest point using circular-dynamics equations.
Thin-film style path difference: two coherent sources with phase difference given directly; find intensity at the point as a fraction of maximum.
A force applied at a point on a rigid body with given r and F vectors; compute torque as cross product and identify the component tending to rotate about a specified axis.
A merry-go-round or turntable with a person walking from rim to centre; apply conservation of angular momentum to find the new angular speed and kinetic-energy change.
Two rods of same material but different lengths and radii conduct heat between the same temperatures; compare thermal resistances or heat currents.
Two identical rods joined end-to-end vs side-by-side between the same baths; compare heat current and equivalent thermal resistance in the two arrangements.
A bullet embeds in a block hanging on a string; combine perfectly-inelastic collision momentum conservation with subsequent pendulum rise to find bullet speed.
Sample activity measured at two instants; deduce half-life from the ratio and predict activity at a later time.
Given atomic masses of parent and daughter nuclei plus the alpha particle, compute the Q-value of alpha decay in MeV from mass defect.
A rod rotating about an axis through one end; given angular speed, ask for the ratio of kinetic energies of two equal halves of the rod, or find the speed of a marked point.
A train moves toward then away from a stationary observer sounding a whistle; compare apparent frequencies for approach and recession using the Doppler formula.
A boat crossing a river with given still-water speed and river speed; find heading to reach the opposite point and the time of crossing by solving velocity-vector components.
YDSE with a thin mica sheet covering one slit; find new fringe position/intensity change from the added optical path.
Velocity–time graph of a body made of straight-line segments; find total displacement as area under v-t graph and identify where speed is maximum.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Given a P-V cycle (triangle/trapezium shaped), compute net work done as area of the loop and heat absorbed per cycle using the first law over the full cycle.
Two blocks connected by a light string over a smooth pulley (Atwood); write free-body equations and find acceleration and tension, then use kinematics for velocity after a given drop.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: A spring balance or lift problem: find normal reaction reading when the lift accelerates up/down with given acceleration.
A projectile explodes or a ball thrown from a tower with given conditions; use two equations to find time of flight and range, with an intermediate point asked.
A spring-block system stretched differently in two trials; compare maximum speeds or energies delivered using energy conservation.
A particle moves with a given position/velocity time function; compute the force as function of time and identify where the force changes direction.
A uniform wire is stretched to double (or n-times) its length; find new resistance and heat produced when connected to the same source.
Find the percentage change in resistance of a wire when both length and radius change by given percentages, keeping volume or not constant as appropriate.
A cell of given emf connected across an external resistance delivers a terminal voltage; use V = ε − Ir to find internal resistance or current.
A network of identical resistors forming a balanced Wheatstone bridge; simplify by symmetry, find equivalent resistance and current through the galvanometer arm (zero in balanced case).
Three resistors in parallel (or series-parallel mix) across a battery; find current in each branch and total power dissipated.
Two cells of different emfs and internal resistances in parallel across a resistor; find equivalent emf of the combination and current through the external resistor.
A capacitor charged to a given voltage is connected to an identical uncharged capacitor; find final common voltage and fraction of energy lost as heat in the connecting wires.

slots.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slots.brief: Rank four simple alkenes (varying substitution) in order of stability; expect justification via hyperconjugation and heat of hydrogenation.
Ask which of the listed compounds is used as a tranquilizer/hypnotic; include barbiturate and analgesic look-alikes as distractors.
Give three-four statements on components, formation conditions and oxidant character of photochemical smog (vs classical smog); ask which are correct.
Multi-statement item on water-soluble vs fat-soluble vitamins, deficiency diseases and whether specific vitamins are synthesised in the body; pick the correct combination.
Show several orderings of elements by electron gain enthalpy (including Cl vs F and positive values for noble gases); identify the incorrect one.
Compare ionic, covalent and interstitial hydrides via multiple statements (reducing nature, thermal stability, reaction with water); ask which set is correct, touching H2O2 stability as distractor.

Provide the figure of d-orbital splitting (octahedral) with electron occupancy for a given metal ion; ask to match it with the correct complex from options and state high/low spin and magnetic character.
Reversible gas-phase dissociation at known total equilibrium pressure; set up ICE table and compute degree of dissociation then Kp.
Compare energy of an electron in a given orbit of a hydrogen-like ion with the corresponding orbit in hydrogen; ask for the ratio in terms of Z and n.
First-order decomposition with known rate constant; compute fraction remaining after a given number of half-lives or time to reach a stated percentage completion.
Ask for the shape and hybridisation of a xenon fluoride/oxide species (e.g. square planar XeF4-type) using lone pair counting.
Give a target ether and ask which alkyl halide + alkoxide combination is correct, including one option that fails due to elimination with a secondary/tertiary halide.
Two gases effuse through the same pinhole in the same time; set up the Graham's law ratio and find the unknown molar mass.
Present a Fischer projection of a molecule with two stereocentres and ask how many R/S configurations and stereoisomers result; test the Fischer-to-R/S rule.
Ask the number of octahedral and tetrahedral voids per unit cell / per atom in an fcc lattice.
Ask which substance acts as a protective colloid (gold number concept) for lyophobic sols such as gold sol.
Show an energy-level diagram of the hydrogen atom with several downward transitions marked; identify which arrow belongs to the Balmer/Lyman series and rank the emitted wavelengths.
Describe turbidity appearance times for three alcohol classes with Lucas reagent; ask to match an alcohol to its observation.
Given a standard cell potential, compute ΔG° and the equilibrium constant of the cell reaction using ΔG° = −nFE° = −RT ln K.
Give the electronic configuration of a lanthanide/transition ion in its ground state; count unpaired electrons and compute the spin-only or effective magnetic moment.
Provide the structure of a branched compound with a functional group and multiple identical substituents; ask for the correct IUPAC name including lowest-locant rules.
A combustion reaction at a given temperature with known ΔU or ΔH; use the gas stoichiometry to convert between ΔH and ΔU.
Figure shows a haloalkane substrate; sequence: alcoholic KOH (E2), then HBr addition (Markovnikov), then aqueous KOH substitution; ask for the final product structure.
Figure shows an aromatic aldehyde lacking alpha-hydrogen treated with concentrated alkali; ask for the alcohol and acid products formed.
Figure shows a cyclic or branched alkene; predict the carbonyl fragments obtained on reductive ozonolysis.
Rank the van 't Hoff factors of a sugar solution and two electrolytes of different stoichiometry (e.g. 1:1 vs 2:1 salts) in water; test the i = number of ions idea.
Given average bond enthalpies of all bonds broken and formed, compute the enthalpy of reaction for a simple gas-phase reaction.
Given limiting molar conductivities of a strong acid, its sodium salt and sodium hydroxide, calculate Λ°m of the weak acid by linear combination.
Ask for the molecular geometry of two-three species with lone pairs (e.g. ammonia-like and water-like); identify correct shapes from options.
Order a primary aliphatic amine, a secondary amine, an aryl amine and ammonia by basic strength in aqueous solution; include steric and solvation effects.
Rank given haloalkanes by SN1 rate, driven by carbocation stability (including a resonance-stabilised arylmethyl case).
Set of statements on why nitrogen differs from heavier group-15 elements (no d-orbitals, small size, N2 triple bond, lack of catenation); ask which combination of statements is valid.
Give a straightforward octahedral complex formula and ask for its correct IUPAC name, with ligand-alphabetical-order distractors.
Rank bond order/bond length of a given bond (e.g. C–O or N–O) across a molecule and its resonance-related ions; ask for the correct increasing bond-length order.
Compare two octahedral complexes of the same metal with a weak-field and a strong-field ligand; state which is paramagnetic with how many unpaired electrons.
Ask which statements about rhombic vs monoclinic sulphur are correct (stability range, transition temperature, S8 ring).
Mix volumes of two solutions (an acid and a base of unequal basicity) and compute the molarity of the excess species left in the final mixture.
Given the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt of type AB2, compute Ksp including the common-ion-free stoichiometric exponents.
Ask which transition metal ion is colourless in aqueous solution and why (d0 or d10 configuration), with coloured d-partly-filled ions as distractors.

slots.subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg
slots.brief: Ask which property is shared by Li and Mg but not by Li and other alkali metals (e.g. nitride formation / carbonate decomposition); match the diagonal-pair property.
Four-part sentence with a subtle subject-verb agreement error (collective noun / distance-quantity subject); one option must be 'No error'.
High-difficulty double-blank sentence where two advanced words must both fit context and tone; distractors are near-synonyms of each blank individually.
Sentence using wrong preposition/gerund construction (e.g. 'capable to' instead of 'capable of'); choose the grammatically improved version.
5-sentence coherent paragraph on a general topic with one sentence clearly the opener; identify which sentence comes first.
Single-blank sentence with a straightforward contextual clue pointing to a common word; options are everyday-level vocabulary.

slots.subtopic: Active and passive voice - complex sentences
slots.brief: Convert a sentence with two clauses and mixed tenses (one passive clause in past perfect) into active voice; watch tricky verb forms and pronoun shifts.
Ask for the synonym of a moderately common word (e.g. 'ardent' level); give it in a short sentence so meaning is testable.
Sentence with a tense inconsistency across clauses (e.g. present perfect paired wrongly with simple past time adverb); pick the corrected version.
Ask for the antonym of a common word used in a short context sentence; ensure distractors are unrelated in meaning.
Give an idiom used in a sentence and ask for its meaning; choose a frequently tested one like 'to burn the midnight oil'.
Short 4-part sentence (P, Q, R, S) that must be rearranged into a grammatical whole; options give order combinations.
Simple sentence testing 'used to' vs 'be used to' or a basic preposition; one clearly correct option at this level.
Present an advanced/literary word in context and ask for its closest meaning; distractors should be plausible but incorrect shades of meaning.
Two/three statements about doctors, artists and painters; ask which conclusions definitely/sossibly follow, including a possibility statement.
Given how a word is coded using letters mapped to numbers based on a discoverable rule, find the code for a new word.
Number pair analogy where relatedness comes from digit/letter positional values (e.g., product of positions or differences); pick the analogous pair.
Alpha-numeric series combining letter shifts and number patterns across terms; find the next term.
Pointing-introduction style chain ('He is the son of my grandfather's only son'); determine the exact relationship between speaker and person.
Given a long word, ask how many meaningful words of N or more letters can be formed (or whether specific words can be formed) using its letters without repetition.
Four word pairs (e.g., state:capital type); three share a hidden relationship and one does not — identify the odd pair with justification.
Find the joint equation of the two lines through origin that are perpendicular to the two lines given by a combined second-degree equation; ask which reduced pair matches.
Given sum of a few terms of an AP, compute a specific later term; keep numbers small.
Direct distance-formula question: distance between two given points in space, answer as an integer after simplification.
Two events with given probabilities and intersection; find P(A | not B) — simple conditional computation.
Find the interval in which a polynomial (factored form) is strictly increasing; test derivative sign.
Indefinite integral of the form f(sin x + cos x) cos x that resolves by a simple substitution; give integrand as combination of sin and cos.
Given a complex number in x+iy form, compute |z| and z̄, then evaluate an expression like z·z̄ or z/z̄ as a+ib.
Direct scalar triple product of three given simple vectors; ask the numeric value or whether they are coplanar.
Indeterminate sin-over-linear form; evaluate using the standard limit sin θ/θ after a small factoring step.
Two lines in space given in symmetric form; use the determinant/coplanarity test to check whether they intersect.
Given eccentricity and a focus (or a vertex and focus), write the equation of an ellipse in standard form; pick gentle numbers.
Solve dy/dx = f(y/x) type homogeneous DE with a simple rational f; general solution with a log.

slots.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slots.brief: Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from a given point to a line given in symmetric form.
Number of onto functions from a set of m elements to a set of n elements via inclusion–exclusion; m and n small enough for a neat answer.
Definite integral of odd function over symmetric interval, or even-function split; require recognition step plus a standard result.
Integral that needs one application of integration by parts (log or inverse-trig times algebraic); ask the antiderivative.
Sum of a series whose nth term is of the form 1/(n(n+k)); telescope to get a closed form in n.
Evaluate a 3×3 determinant of small integers and/or use it to decide a matrix property (singular or not).
Vector triple product expression a × (b × c) with given simple vectors; use the standard expansion and compute the result vector.
Binomial situation: given n and p (as fractions), compute mean and/or variance of the distribution; single-formula numerical.
Form 4-digit numbers from given digits with a divisibility or ordering restriction; case-wise counting with small digit set.
Definite integral reduced by a trigonometric/half-angle substitution (e.g. sin x or tan(x/2) substitution) leading to a log or standard value.
Line with unknown slope parameter touches a given circle; use distance from centre = radius to find the parameter (or equation of tangent from a point).
Given two explicit functions as sets of pairs or formulas, decide which statements about f∘g, g∘f or injectivity/surjectivity are true.
Find the term independent of x (or coefficient of x^k) in the expansion of a binomial with positive integral power; standard general-term matching.
Solve an equation like sin θ = cos θ or a simple compound-angle equation and give the general solution.
Arrangement of letters of a word with two specific people/letters never adjacent; total arrangements minus the fused-block count.
Given z subject to a modulus condition like |z - z₁| = |z - z₂| or |z| = r, identify the locus/interpretation (perpendicular bisector/circle) and answer a numeric or conceptual MCQ.
For a 2×2 or 3×3 matrix A satisfying a relation like A² = I or A² = A + I, compute A⁵ or A⁶ as a linear combination of A and I.
Find the equation of a circle through three given points, or of a circle with given centre and passing through a point; complete-the-square optional.
Directly solve a simple separable first-order DE of the form dy/dx = f(x)g(y) with standard integral on each side; find the general solution.
Statement-correctness question on symmetric/skew matrices and transpose rules (e.g. AB = (BA)ᵀ iff…); pick the true statement among four.
Find the range or positivity condition of a quadratic/rational expression via discriminant or completing the square; answer the set of values.
Classical probability with dice or balls: single-event probability from a small sample space; one-step count.
Composite evaluation: sin⁻¹/cos⁻¹ of a value leading to a triangle-based simplification, e.g. tan(sin⁻¹(x)) style; give answer in exact form.
Piecewise function with a parameter; find the parameter so that the function is continuous (and check differentiability if 5/5); match one-sided limits at the joint.
Evaluate a given sin/cos of a sum/difference using compound-angle formulae; ask for the numeric value among options.
Given a relation between roots (or one root given), find the value of k or another root using the root equation plus Vieta's relations.
Use differentials to approximate the value of √(near a perfect square) or a similar function at a nearby point.
Effect of adding a constant (or scaling) on mean and variance of a data set; ask the new mean and SD.
Locate the local maxima/minima of a cubic (or trig on an interval) using derivative sign change; ask the value of the function at the extremum.
Rational function with a quadratic denominator; resolve into partial fractions (repeated linear factor) and integrate.

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image of a given point in a given line using the reflection formula; identify the correct image coordinates.
Domain of a function involving a square root and a log/denominator (e.g. √(linear) / log(x - a)); intersect the constraints and choose the set.
For a curve given implicitly (e.g. xy = k or x² + xy + y² = c), find dy/dx at a given point or the slope of the tangent there.
